title: TurboSpec: Closed-loop Speculation Control System for Optimizing LLM Serving Goodput
technique: closed-loop control of speculation length per step in vLLM using offline-profiled batch latency model plus online acceptance-rate feedback to maximize goodput; disables speculation at high load

optimized_metrics.evidence: TurboSpec predicts "goodput"—the amount of successfully generated tokens— to evaluate and adjust intra-request parallelism amount to that with the highest goodput in runtime.

headline_claim.text: TurboSpec ... demonstrate its effectiveness across diverse workloads and hardware configurations, providing consistent performance improvements across all test scenarios.

reported_metrics.where: Tables 4-5 average request latency (s); Fig 13-14 request latency CDF under QPS/dataset shifts; headline only (re-pass)
Fig 9-10 speedup = non-spec / spec latency per request across batch sizes 1-64
Fig 11 offline throughput speedup (spec / non-spec), up to ~2x on L40S

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Goodput = Number of Generated Tokens / Execution Time (1) i.e., goodput counts only the tokens that contribute to the final output: the validated speculative and bonus tokens.
metric_definitions.notes: NOT the SLO-attainment goodput of DistServe etc.: no SLO involved; it is correct-token rate, equal to throughput when no speculation ("in the absence of speculative decoding, the goodput and throughput are the same", §1). Estimated per step as accept_len / batch_latency

metric_definitions.definition_quote: we measure speedup as the ratio between non-speculative and speculative decoding latency per request.
metric_definitions.notes: average request latency over 10 profiling iterations

metric_definitions.definition_quote: we measure the average request latency across varying batch sizes using real datasets
metric_definitions.notes: per-request end-to-end latency; not formally defined; no TTFT/TPOT

load_regime: static fixed batch sizes (1-64) and dynamic request-rate (QPS) changes plus dataset-distribution shift; online serving in vLLM; separate offline throughput test
tradeoff_acknowledged: Occasional degradation: Vicuna-33B at QPS=16 average request latency 43.32s original vs 46.16s TurboSpec. Speculation is harmful at high load / low acceptance, so it is throttled or disabled.
models: Llama2-7B (draft Llama-160M), Llama3-8B/70B, Vicuna-33B; methods: draft model, prompt lookup, EAGLE
extractor_notes: Two-column layout garbled by pdftotext; line refs approximate. Title/abstract 'goodput' means correct tokens/s, unrelated to SLO. The system's actual objective is a throughput-like quantity (goodput) used as a proxy to reduce request latency; headline abstract gives no numeric result. Only mean latency, no tail percentiles (CDFs shown only).
load_class_quote: For the static setting, we measure the average request latency across varying batch sizes using real datasets ... dynamic QPS; online serving under varying request rates (§7) plus fixed batch sizes 1-64 (§6) and offline throughput test (Fig 11)
repass_log: E2E: result-only (average request latency in §7 results); no design statement for request latency (design target is goodput); demoted to reported_metrics
